annotations.title: What does this college athletics program earn and spend, sport by sport, against its peers?

description: Use when the user is an athletic director, conference or university finance staff, or a sponsor, apparel or media partner sizing a college program: "how much does Texas athletics bring in?", "how dependent is this school on football?", "where does our program rank in the Big Ten?". Returns one NCAA Division I school's reported athletics revenue and expenses for 2024-25, split by football, men's and women's basketball, other men's and women's sports and not allocated; football and men's basketball as a share of revenue allocated to sports; athletes per sport; and its rank and the median in its Division I classification or in the schools you name. EADA has no conference field, so for a conference, name its members. Refuses before you are charged if the school is not an exact match, and lists candidates. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Dimensions (vary these inputs to cut the answer; each call is its own run): over time: one EADA data year; compare: compare (2-20 schools) or the school's Division I classification; segment: sport; men and women (in the result). Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound. For listed sports companies rather than schools, use run_sports_business_benchmark.

compare.description: Optional: 2-20 schools to compare with, e.g. a conference's members, by name or UNITID. Leave out to compare with the school's own classification (FBS, FCS or Division I without football).

school.description: A Division I school's name as IPEDS lists it (e.g. "University of Texas at Austin") or its 6-digit UNITID (e.g. "228778").
